question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, how long must a principal or supervising broker retain each brokerage agreement, from the date of execution?
choice_a: One year
choice_b: Two years
choice_c: Three years
choice_d: Five years
explanation: Each brokerage agreement, and each disclosure/consent to dual or designated agency, must be retained for three years from the date of execution.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, how long must transaction documents (executed contracts of sale, leases, settlement statements) be retained, and from what date?
choice_a: One year from the date of listing
choice_b: Seven years from the date of closing
choice_c: Five years from the date of closing
choice_d: Three years from the date of closing, or from ratification if the transaction fails to close
explanation: Transaction documents must be retained for three years from the date of closing, or from ratification if the transaction fails to close.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, what financial-record information must a principal broker maintain regarding real estate transactions?
choice_a: From whom money was received, the date of receipt, place and date of deposit, and final disposition of funds
choice_b: Only the final sale price
choice_c: Only the buyer's name and address
choice_d: Only records related to commission splits
explanation: The principal broker must maintain financial records showing from whom money was received, the date of receipt, place and date of deposit, and the final disposition of the funds.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-185, if a principal broker's office is located outside Virginia but the firm has a Virginia branch office, what must be true of the required records?
choice_a: Records need not be kept for the Virginia branch at all
choice_b: A copy of the records must be readily accessible in the Virginia office
choice_c: Records may be kept exclusively at the out-of-state office with no Virginia copy
choice_d: Records must be filed annually with the Virginia Real Estate Board instead of kept at the office
explanation: When the principal broker's office is outside Virginia and the firm has a Virginia branch office, a copy of the required records must be readily accessible in the Virginia office.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-190, all advertising by a firm or affiliated licensee must be under whose direct supervision, and in whose name?
choice_a: The individual licensee's supervision, in the licensee's personal name
choice_b: The Real Estate Board's supervision, in the Board's name
choice_c: The principal broker or supervising broker's supervision, in the name of the firm
choice_d: No supervision is required for online advertising
explanation: All advertising must be under the direct supervision of the principal broker or supervising broker, in the name of the firm, with the firm's licensed name clearly and legibly displayed.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-190(B), what must all advertising by a firm or affiliated licensee clearly, legibly, and conspicuously contain?
choice_a: The listing price only
choice_b: A copy of the brokerage agreement
choice_c: The licensee's personal cell phone number only
choice_d: An advertising disclosure including the firm's name and office contact information
explanation: All advertising must contain a clear, legible, conspicuous disclosure including the firm's name and office contact information, per the firm's written policies.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-190(B)(4), when must advertising be updated?
choice_a: In a timely manner whenever there is a material change to the listing status or property description
choice_b: Only at the start of each calendar year
choice_c: Advertising never needs to be updated once posted
choice_d: Only when the client specifically requests an update
explanation: Advertising must be updated in a timely manner whenever there is a material change to the listing status or property descriptions.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-220(A), a disclosure of brokerage relationship in a purchase transaction generally must be made in writing no later than what point?
choice_a: Only at closing
choice_b: No later than the time specific real estate assistance is first provided
choice_c: Within 30 days after the transaction closes
choice_d: There is no timing requirement
explanation: The disclosure must be made in writing at the earliest practical time, but no later than the time specific real estate assistance is first provided.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-220(A)(3), a licensee acting as a dual or designated agent must obtain written consent from all clients by what point relative to the buyer's offer?
choice_a: Consent is never required for designated agents
choice_b: Only after the offer is accepted
choice_c: Not later than the time an offer to purchase is presented to the licensee who will present it to the listing agent or seller
choice_d: Within 10 days after closing
explanation: Written consent must be obtained from the buyer no later than when the offer to purchase is presented to the licensee who will present it to the listing agent or seller, and from the seller no later than when the offer is presented to the seller.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-220(B), does the lease-transaction brokerage-relationship disclosure requirement apply to residential leases under two months?
choice_a: Yes, it applies to all leases regardless of term
choice_b: It applies only if the tenant requests disclosure
choice_c: It applies only to commercial leases under two months
choice_d: No, it does not apply to lessors or lessees in single or multi-family residential units for lease terms of less than two months
explanation: The lease-transaction disclosure requirement does not apply to lessors/lessees in single or multi-family residential units for lease terms under two months.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-225, when must a principal or supervising broker conduct (or have conducted) a mandatory audit of the firm's practices?
choice_a: Within 90 days prior to the expiration of the firm license
choice_b: Only once, when the firm first licenses
choice_c: Every 10 years
choice_d: Only if a complaint has been filed against the firm
explanation: A principal broker or supervising broker must conduct or have a third party conduct an audit within 90 days prior to the expiration of the firm license, documented on a Board-developed form.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-225, the mandatory audit must examine and document the firm's compliance in which of the following areas?
choice_a: Only tax filings
choice_b: Handling of escrow deposits, fair housing compliance, and advertising, among other matters
choice_c: Only the number of transactions closed that year
choice_d: Only employee performance reviews
explanation: The audit must examine compliance with escrow deposit handling, fair housing laws (for firms doing residential business), advertising, and other listed matters.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.1, what disclosure-related form must the Real Estate Board develop and maintain on its website for residential transactions?
choice_a: A criminal background check waiver
choice_b: A commission-splitting agreement template
choice_c: A residential property disclosure statement form
choice_d: A mortgage pre-approval form
explanation: The Board must develop a residential property disclosure statement form for use under the Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Act and maintain it on its website.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2105.1, in addition to the disclosure statement, what one-page form must the Board also develop and maintain?
choice_a: A form transferring title
choice_b: A form waiving the buyer's right to inspection
choice_c: A form authorizing dual agency automatically
choice_d: A form for the purchaser to acknowledge being advised of the disclosures on the disclosure statement
explanation: The Board must also develop and maintain a one-page form signed by the parties acknowledging the purchaser has been advised of the disclosures listed in the residential property disclosure statement.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2131(B), how must a seller's licensee make the required disclosure of material adverse facts about the physical condition of a property?
choice_a: In writing
choice_b: Verbally only, at the first showing
choice_c: By posting a sign on the property
choice_d: There is no specific format required
explanation: A seller's licensee's disclosure of material adverse facts pertaining to the physical condition of the property must be made in writing.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2133(B), if a licensee engaged by a landlord has actual knowledge of plumbing that does not meet the federal Safe Drinking Water Act's 'lead free' definition in a residential property, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Nothing; this is outside the scope of disclosure duties
choice_b: Disclose it to the prospective tenant
choice_c: Disclose it only to the landlord, never the tenant
choice_d: Replace the plumbing before leasing
explanation: If a landlord's licensee has actual knowledge of non-lead-free plumbing components in a residential property, the licensee must disclose this to the prospective tenant.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-220(A)(4), if a brokerage-relationship disclosure is combined with other disclosures or information, how must it be presented?
choice_a: In the same font and size as all other text, with no distinction required
choice_b: In a footnote at the bottom of the document
choice_c: Conspicuously -- printed in bold lettering, all capitals, underlined, or in a separate box
choice_d: It cannot be combined with other disclosures under any circumstance
explanation: If combined with other information, the disclosure must be conspicuous -- printed in bold, all caps, underlined, or set off in a separate box.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-190(B)(3), if a licensee discovers that a third party controls advertising containing inaccurate property information, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Nothing; third-party advertising is not the licensee's responsibility
choice_b: Cancel the listing agreement immediately
choice_c: Report the third party to the Attorney General
choice_d: Make a timely written request for changes to be made
explanation: A licensee who knows or discovers a third party controls advertising with inaccurate or outdated information must make a timely written request for changes.

question: Under 18VAC135-20-185(B), what must a principal broker maintain in addition to the specific records listed, to demonstrate compliance?
choice_a: A bookkeeping or recordkeeping system with accounting records in sufficient detail to determine compliance
choice_b: A separate legal opinion letter for every transaction
choice_c: Nothing further is required beyond the specific listed records
choice_d: A notarized statement from every client
explanation: The principal broker must maintain a bookkeeping/recordkeeping system with accounting records in sufficient detail to determine compliance with recordkeeping requirements.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2135(C), if a licensee managing a property also represents the owner as seller or landlord, what must the licensee do?
choice_a: Nothing further is needed
choice_b: Disclose the brokerage relationships pursuant to the provisions of the article
choice_c: Terminate the property management agreement first
choice_d: Obtain a separate license for each role
explanation: A licensee may represent the owner as seller or landlord in addition to managing the property if they enter a brokerage relationship for that role, disclosing the relationships per the article.

question: Under VA Code 54.1-2131(F), does a seller's licensee have to disclose whether settlement services will be provided by an attorney versus a nonattorney settlement agent?
choice_a: Yes, this must always be disclosed in writing
choice_b: Only in transactions over $1,000,000
choice_c: No, nothing in this section requires such disclosure
choice_d: Only if using a nonattorney agent
explanation: VA Code 54.1-2131(F) states nothing in that section requires a licensee to disclose whether settlement services under Title 55.1 Chapter 10 will be provided by an attorney or nonattorney settlement agent.
